About Us
The Alchemy Atelier is an architecture and interior design studio driven by curiosity, creativity and purpose. Every project is drawn slowly, built carefully and finished with materials chosen to age well.
We collaborate closely with our clients to understand their story, their dreams and their lifestyle transforming them into timeless spaces that are beautiful, functional and deeply personal.

Photo: A pen and ink sketch of a classical doorway: fanlight, fluted columns, wall lanterns and clipped bay trees in urns
Our Vision
Spaces that matter
We envision spaces that elevate everyday life, inspire well-being and leave a positive legacy.
Everyday life • Well-being • Legacy
Photo: A pencil sketch of a living room: a linen sofa under four framed botanical prints, a fiddle-leaf fig in a terracotta pot, a round table on a patterned rug and a tall arched window
Our Philosophy
Beauty in balance
We believe that timeless design emerges when form, function and emotion exist in perfect harmony.
Form • Function • Emotion

Our Process
Six stages, from the first conversation to the day you move in.
Discovery
We start by listening. How you live, what the space has to hold, and the budget it sits inside.
Concept development
Mood boards, palettes and first directions, until the scheme reads like you rather than like us.
Space planning
Layouts drawn and redrawn: circulation, sightlines, and where the light falls through the day.
Material selection
Finishes chosen in the hand rather than off a screen: stone, timber, fabric and paint, seen together.
Design detailing
Joinery, lighting and fittings drawn to the millimetre, down to the last handle and hinge.
Execution & handover
One team on site and one line of accountability, through the snag list to the day we hand you the keys.

Our Services
Four ways to work with the studio, from a whole building to a single piece. Whichever you choose, the same hands draw it and see it through to site.

One Pair of Hands
Same vision. Deeper attention.
Principal Architect and Design Futurist
Jemima Francis
An architect, interior designer and curator based in Hyderabad, Jemima leads The Alchemy Atelier on the belief that thoughtful design can change the way we live, feel and belong.
From architecture and interiors through to curation, every project is personally drawn and personally seen through, so the journey from concept to completion stays in one pair of hands. No hand-offs, no juniors learning on your home: the person you meet at the first conversation is the person on site at the last.
Architecture Interiors Consultancy
“Design, for me, is a dialogue between people, places and possibilities.”
Ar. Jemima Francis

Why choose us
We believe that a great design is a collaboration of ideas, vision and trust. Here is what sets the studio apart.
Transparent pricing
Detailed quotations, clear material specifications and honest budgeting at every stage. No hidden costs.
In-house design team
Your drawings are developed under one roof by our own architects and interior designers.
The same person throughout
Whoever you speak to first is the one who draws the work, prices it and meets you on site. Nothing is handed on.
Regular progress updates
Structured updates from site, so you always know what is happening and what comes next.
Quality vendor network
Skilled craftsmen and suppliers chosen for workmanship, because a good design still needs skilled hands.
End-to-end turnkey service
From the first sketch to the final styling, managed as one project with one line of accountability.

What are you looking for?
Eight ways the studio works, and most projects want more than one. Tick whatever sounds like yours, as many as you like, and it travels into the message with you, so you never have to explain it twice.
Architecture
Ground up homes, additions and adaptive reuse, drawn from the first sketch through to the last handle.
Construction
The site run by the studio: contractors, sequence and quality all held to the drawing.
Interiors
Layouts, joinery, materials and lighting resolved as one scheme, not a series of purchases.
Consultancy
A second pair of eyes on a project already moving: feasibility, palettes, drawings, approvals.
Design
Furniture, objects and the details around them, drawn for the room they belong to.
Modular
Kitchens and wardrobes built off site to the millimetre, then fitted without a mark on the wall.
Turnkey
One contract for the whole of it: we take the drawing, the trades and the site, and hand back the keys.
Execution
Drawings made into built work: procurement, the order of the trades, finishing and snagging.
We’ve got you.

Featured Projects
Every room has a story.
The Gallery
A selection of houses, rooms and objects the studio has drawn and seen through to site. Each one began with a conversation, and ended with a set of keys.

Project: The Palm Wall
Interiors · Private residence · 2026
A closer look at the shelving. Each shelf carries its own strip of light, so what sits on it is lit the way a gallery would light it.
Palm leaf wallpaper held between warm timber: open shelving lit from within on one side, a tall cabinet on the other, and a floating console that ties the two together.

Project: The Lantern Wall
Interiors · Private residence · 2026
Soft panels with light drawn along their seams, a fluted door that disappears into the wall, and a low floating console under the screen.
The same wall from the dining table. The light runs through the joinery rather than hanging in front of it, so the wall is lit from within.

Project: The Emerald Drawing Room
Interiors · Dehradun · 2025
A single deep green carried from the plaster to the velvet, warmed with hammered brass so the room reads as one material rather than a set of purchases.

Project: House of Arches
Architecture · Mussoorie · 2023
Hand plastered openings that step down the slope, each one framing the next, and a timber door at the end of the run to catch the afternoon.

Project: The Green Room
Interiors · Dehradun · 2024
A sage wall, cane joinery and a round mirror placed where the morning light lands. Planted heavily, on purpose.

Project: The Brick Arcade
Architecture · Rajpur Road, Dehradun · 2024
An arcade of arched openings holding a planted courtyard, drawn so the brick does the shading and the building needs less of everything else.

Project: Vessels, a Series
Design · Studio edition · 2025
Stone vessels turned for a particular plinth in a particular room, then made again as a small edition because they refused to stay one of a kind.

Project: Terracotta House
Interiors · Doon Valley · 2023
Earth tones taken from the site itself: terracotta plaster, a low timber line, and lighting resolved with the layout rather than after it.

Project: Courtyard of Stones
Architecture · Rishikesh · 2022
A stone archway that keeps the courtyard cool and the house quiet, built with local masons who knew the stone better than any drawing did.

Project: The Reading Corner
Interiors · Dehradun · 2025
One chair, one lamp, one window. The smallest commission the studio has taken, and the one most often asked after.

Project: Still Life in Green
Design · Studio edition · 2024
A ribbed vase, a brass tray and a candle: objects drawn for the room they belong to, and made to last longer than the scheme around them.

Service 03
From the first sketch to the last handle.
Architecture
Ground up homes, additions and adaptive reuse. Drawn from the first sketch through to the last handle, and seen through the approvals and the site in between.

What this covers
The whole of a building project, from the first read of the site to the last visit while it goes up. Taken together, or joined at any stage.
Feasibility and a read of the site What the plot allows, what it faces, and what is realistic, before you commit to a brief or a budget.
Concept, then drawings developed in full The idea settled first as plan and massing, then developed until every dimension and junction is decided.
Planning and building regulations The drawings and documents the approvals ask for, prepared, submitted, and followed through the questions that come back.
Tender packages and contractor selection A package complete enough for builders to price like for like, and help reading what comes back.
Structural and services coordination Engineers and services consultants brought in early, so structure and drainage are designed with the plan rather than around it.
Site visits through construction Regular visits while it is going up: questions answered, work checked against the drawing, and changes recorded.

Who it suits
Building work begins from very different starting points. These are the three we are asked for most.
Photo: A brick arcade of arched openings onto a planted courtyard
A plot with nothing on it yet
A blank site, where orientation, access and levels shape the house long before a wall is drawn.
Photo: A planted courtyard seen through a stone archway
An extension the existing house has to absorb
New work that has to read as though it was always there, in scale, in material, and in the way the light moves.
Photo: A room lit from a tall window onto planting
An old building asked to do something new
A change of use or a reworked plan, done with respect for what is worth keeping and honest about what is not.

How it runs
Six stages, from the first look at the plot to the day the scaffolding comes down.
Site
What the plot allows, what it faces, and what the light does across the day.
Feasibility
What can be built, what it is likely to cost, and what the approvals will ask for.
Concept
The plan and the massing settled before any detail is drawn.
Approvals
Planning and building regulations drawings, submitted and followed through.
Tender
A package a contractor can price, and help choosing between them.
Construction
Site visits, queries answered, and the work checked as it goes up.

Service 04
A second pair of eyes.
Consultancy
A second pair of eyes on a project already moving, from a studio you are not committing the whole job to.

Service 02
Drawn for the room it stands in.
Furniture Design
Furniture and objects drawn for the room they belong to. Prototyped with the workshops we work with, detailed down to the hardware, and made to outlast the scheme around them.

What this covers
From the first sketch to the piece standing in the room, drawn and detailed closely enough for a maker to build it exactly.
Bespoke furniture drawn for the room Drawn to the millimetre for the wall it will stand against, in the proportion the room asks for.
Joinery details, hardware and edges How it opens, what holds it together, and how the edge feels under a hand: decided rather than defaulted.
Prototypes made with our workshops A piece worth making twice is worth mocking up first. Proportion and comfort are tested before good material is cut.
Material and finish samples Timber, veneer, stone, metal and fabric seen in the hand and in the room’s own light before anything is ordered.
Drawings a maker can build from Full workshop drawings with sizes, sections and finishes, so the piece can be priced and built without guesswork.
Delivery, fitting and aftercare Brought in, levelled and fitted by people who know the drawing, with a word afterwards on how to look after it.

Who it suits
Furniture is commissioned for a reason. These are the three we hear most often.
Photo: A quiet room with a tan leather armchair and a paper lamp
A piece that has to fit an awkward space
A sloping ceiling, a chimney breast, a run that stops short. Nothing off a shelf will sit right in it.
Photo: A low linen sofa against a terracotta plaster wall
A set of pieces that should read as a family
Different rooms, one hand: a shared timber, a shared detail, a shared proportion, without everything matching.
Photo: A cane sideboard below a round mirror
Replacing something bought that never quite worked
The size was wrong, or the finish, or the way it opened. This time it is drawn around the actual use.

How it runs
Six stages from brief to delivery, each one settled before the next begins.
Brief
What the piece has to do, where it stands, and what it sits beside.
Drawing
Proportion and profile settled on paper before anything is cut.
Materials
Timber, stone, metal and fabric chosen in the hand, with samples to approve.
Prototype
A trial piece or a mock up where the detail warrants one.
Making
Built by the workshops we work with, to drawings they can build from.
Delivery
Fitted in place, with the care it will need afterwards written down.

Service 01
One scheme, not a set of purchases.
Interior Design
Whole interiors resolved as one scheme. The plan, the joinery, the materials and the light are considered together, so a room reads as a single idea rather than a series of things bought separately and asked to get along.

What this covers
Everything that goes into resolving a room, from the plan down to the last handle. Most projects want all of it, and some want only a part.
Space planning and circulation Where the walls, doors and openings want to be, and how you move between them, settled before anything is chosen.
Joinery designed and drawn in detail Wardrobes, kitchens and built-in storage drawn as part of the room rather than ordered from a catalogue.
Materials, finishes and colour Stone, timber, tile, fabric and paint chosen together and seen side by side, so nothing is decided in isolation.
Lighting layouts, fittings and controls Where the light falls, what casts it, and which switch does what, planned early while the wiring can still move.
Furniture, fabric and final styling Loose furniture, soft furnishings and the last layer of objects, specified so the finished room is not left to chance.
Site coordination through the fit out We hold the drawing on site: answering the trades, checking work as it goes up, and snagging what is not right.

Who it suits
Interiors work starts from different places. These are the three we are asked for most often.
Photo: A living room in earthy tones with a terracotta plaster wall
A whole home, or one room done properly
There is no minimum. One room resolved properly is better work than a whole house done thinly.
Photo: A living room with a sage green wall, a cane sideboard and large plants
A renovation where the layout is being reconsidered
Best caught before the walls come down, while moving a door or a window is still an easy decision.
Photo: A quiet room with a tan leather armchair and a paper lamp
A house that is built but has never been finished
The shell is up and the rooms are empty. We pick it up from there and take it through to lived in.

How it runs
Six stages, in order, so you always know what has just been decided and what comes next.
Discovery
We start by listening. How you live, what the space has to hold, and the budget it sits inside.
Concept
Mood boards, palettes and first directions, until the scheme reads like you rather than like us.
Space planning
Layouts drawn and redrawn: circulation, sightlines, and where the light falls through the day.
Materials
Finishes chosen in the hand rather than off a screen: stone, timber, fabric and paint, seen together.
Detailing
Joinery, lighting and fittings drawn to the millimetre, down to the last handle and hinge.
Execution
One team on site and one line of accountability, through the snag list to the day we hand you the keys.
